concept.name: Reg SHO
concept.definition: The SEC's short-sale regulation (Rules 200-204 under the Exchange Act), adopted in 2004 with compliance beginning January 3, 2005, to update short-sale regulation and address abusive naked short selling and persistent failures to deliver. Its four pillars are order marking (Rule 200), the short-sale price test circuit breaker (Rule 201), the locate requirement (Rule 203(b)), and close-out requirements for fails to deliver (Rules 204 and 203(b)(3)).
concept.intuition: It's the rulebook that keeps short selling honest: mark your orders correctly, don't pile onto crashing stocks, line up shares before you sell, and actually deliver what you sold.
concept.mechanics: Rule 200 requires sale orders to be marked 'long,' 'short,' or 'short exempt.' Rule 201 imposes a bid-based price test for a stock down 10% intraday. Rule 203(b) requires a documented locate before shorting and a 13-day close-out for threshold securities; Rule 204 requires clearing-agency participants to close out fails to deliver by the start of the next settlement day (short sales) or third settlement day (long sales/bona fide market making), with pre-borrow penalties otherwise.
concept.failure_modes: Fails to deliver persist for legitimate reasons (processing delays, hard-to-borrow names), so threshold-list inclusion does not prove abuse; the rules also cannot fully prevent manipulation executed through options, offshore venues, or deceptive conduct addressed instead by antifraud Rule 10b-21.
concept.misconceptions: Naked short selling is not categorically illegal under Reg SHO — market makers in bona fide market making may short without a locate; nor does appearing on a threshold securities list brand a company or its stock as manipulated.
concept.example: A broker-dealer that fails to deliver shares from a short sale must buy or borrow like-kind securities to close out the fail by the opening of trading on the next settlement day, or it and its introducing brokers are barred from further short sales in that stock without a pre-borrow.

citations.source: SEC Office of Investor Education and Assistance, Key Points About Regulation SHO
